simple.meaning: נְצַל (nᵉtsal) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to extricate.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 3:29. The surrounding contexts include Torah, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נְצַל (H5338) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: נְצַל (nᵉtsal) / H5338 is traced through Daniel 3:29, Daniel 6:15, Daniel 6:28 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Therefore I make a decree, that every people, nation, and language, which speak anything evil against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, shall be cut in pieces, and their houses shall be made a dunghill; because there is no other god who is able to deliver like this.”

timeline.evidenceText: Therefore I make a decree, that every people, nation, and language, which speak anything evil against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, shall be cut in pieces, and their houses shall be made a dunghill; because there is no other god who is able to deliver like this.”
Then these men assembled together to the king, and said to the king, “Know, O king, that it is a law of the Medes and Persians, that no decree nor statute which the king establishes may be changed.”
So this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
